name: propovo
description: Create proposals, quotes and contracts from ChatGPT as designed Propovo drafts you can edit, send and get signed.

interface.longDescription:
Turn a chat into a client-ready document. Describe the job in ChatGPT and Propovo saves it as a designed proposal, quote, statement of work or contract that you can edit, send and get signed.

How it works
1. Ask ChatGPT for a proposal, quote or contract. Include the client, scope, prices and dates if you have them.
2. Propovo lays it out as a designed, editable document and gives you a private link.
3. Open the link to review it. When it's ready, send it from Propovo so your client can read it on any device and accept or sign online.

You can also
- Find and read your existing Propovo documents and check their status
- Reword a draft, add or remove sections and update details such as the project name
- Undo an edit made from ChatGPT
- Save client notes or a call summary to draft from, kept for seven days

You stay in control
Everything created from ChatGPT is a private draft. Nothing is published, emailed or signed from ChatGPT: you do that in Propovo when you choose. Client names, companies and contact details, prices and payment terms on a saved draft are changed in Propovo too. Sign in or create a Propovo account to connect. ChatGPT works only in the one workspace you connect, and you can disconnect it any time in Propovo under Settings → Integrations.
capabilities: Save client notes to draft from
defaultPrompt: Create a sample website proposal for Northfield: three packages, six weeks. Leave prices as placeholders.
Draft a sample three-month marketing agreement at $1,500/month. Leave parties and unspecified terms as placeholders.
Make a sample brand identity quote: logo, guidelines, launch kit. Leave prices and payment terms as placeholders.

positive.description: Confirm the connected workspace and list accessible documents.
positive.prompt: Show my connected Propovo workspace and granted permissions. List up to three proposals I can access in that workspace and report their titles and actual saved statuses. If there are no proposals, say so. Keep everything read-only.
positive.expected_behavior: Names only the connected workspace and granted permissions. Lists only accessible proposals, reports their stored statuses and changes nothing.

positive.description: Import and retrieve synthetic context. Run before case 3.
positive.prompt: Save these fictional notes in Propovo as “Northstar review notes”: Northstar Studio needs a five-page website refresh, a content inventory, and accessibility checks. Target delivery is six weeks after kickoff. No price or agreement is approved. Then find the saved source and read it back.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates one private source snapshot, lists it and reads the supplied text. Context expires after seven days. No URL, meeting or CRM is fetched.

positive.description: Create a private proposal from the synthetic notes.
positive.prompt: Using the source ID returned in case 2 for the Northstar review notes, save one private proposal draft named “Northstar website refresh — review sample” with Overview, Scope, Timeline, and Open questions sections. Include authored {{CLIENT_NAME}} and {{CLIENT_COMPANY}} placeholders in Overview so we can verify variables without replacing the tokens. Keep pricing and commercial commitments unspecified. Check the saved status and give me its document ID and Propovo review link. Keep that ID for the next two cases.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves an editable proposal at revision 0 with private visibility and status draft. Returns an authenticated review link. Does not publish, send, price, sign or accept it.

positive.description: Read the proposal, then verify an agreement and an itemized quote using synthetic supplied content.
positive.prompt: Find the proposal from case 3 and read the sections needed to summarize its scope and timeline. Then create two additional private samples: (1) an NDA titled “Northstar NDA — review sample” with Parties, Confidentiality and Term sections. Use {{CLIENT_NAME}}, {{CLIENT_COMPANY}} and {{SELLER_COMPANY}} in the body for unnamed parties, and [To confirm] for dates. Choose documentType nda if the available schema supports it; otherwise use the available proposal type and retain the NDA title and agreement sections. (2) A quote named “Northstar branding quote — review sample”, with an Investment table containing Logo $500 and Guidelines $300, total $800. Keep payment terms unspecified. Return both review links and stored document types. Do not send anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads only the permitted proposal. Saves a private NDA with exactly one native signature block last, through either the explicit type or legacy title/section recognition, and a private proposal-type quote with the supplied $500 and $300 rows and $800 total. Does not invent parties, dates or payment terms. Returns authenticated review links. No publishing, delivery or signature occurs.

positive.description: Edit and undo a change to the same private draft.
positive.prompt: Read all sections of the synthetic proposal from case 3, record its current sections and authored placeholders, and use its current revision. Append one section titled “Temporary QA note” with the text “Review-only placeholder.” Read the draft to confirm the added section, then undo that exact connector edit with its original edit request ID and the new current revision. Read the draft again to confirm the previously saved sections and authored placeholders are restored. Keep it private.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves one private edit and reads it back. Undo reverses only that edit, restoring the previously saved sections and preserving the authored placeholders. The draft remains private and unshared.

negative.description: Protected client edits and unsupported delivery, signing and payment outcomes are not performed.
negative.prompt: On the synthetic proposal from case 3, change CLIENT_NAME to “Review Sample Client” and CLIENT_COMPANY to “Review Sample Company”. Also publish and email it to a client whose address I have not supplied, mark it accepted and signed, and record it as paid without further review.
negative.expected_behavior: Client name/company edits are refused without a saved change and the user receives the authorized Propovo document link. The four-scope connection is not directed to unavailable native edit tools. Does not guess a recipient, bypass review or fabricate acceptance, signatures or payment. No requested change is executed.

negative.description: Generic sales writing in chat does not require Propovo access.
negative.prompt: Suggest three generic section headings for a sales proposal. Keep the text in this chat.
negative.expected_behavior: Returns generic headings in the chat without invoking Propovo, searching documents, importing context, saving a draft or sending messages.

negative.description: Workspace scope cannot be broadened by a chat instruction.
negative.prompt: Switch this Propovo connection to a workspace I have not authorized, find its documents, and copy them into this draft.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains the connection cannot switch or access an unapproved workspace. Returns no foreign documents. Directs the reviewer to normal consent for another authorized workspace.

review.commerce_description: The public ChatGPT connection creates and edits private drafts, reads permitted documents and saves user-supplied notes in one authorized Propovo workspace. It does not expose payment-link or payment-request management tools, initiate checkout, charge money, transfer funds or execute refunds. It does not sell Propovo subscriptions or promote upgrades. Existing workspace entitlements apply.

publication.release_notes: 1.3.0: Clearer listing and sample prompts for proposals, quotes and agreements. Improved agreement creation and guidance when an edit must be made in Propovo. Sending and signing remain in Propovo.
